definitions.explanation: A Buddhist monk who studied in Tang China and founded the Shingon school on his return, with its center at {高野山|こうやさん}. Known after his death as {弘法大師|こうぼうだいし}, he is also revered as one of Japan's greatest calligraphers.

examples.japanese: {空海|くうかい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{真言宗|しんごんしゅう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|ひら}いた→開く：01979_hiraku⟧。
{空海|くうかい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{唐|とう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{密教|みっきょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{学|まな}んだ→学ぶ：01987_manabu⟧。
examples.english: Kūkai studied esoteric Buddhism in Tang China.

examples.japanese: ⟦{四国|しこく}→四国：21447_shikoku⟧{遍路|へんろ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{空海|くうかい}⟦ゆかり→ゆかり：10650_yukari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧88⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{寺|てら}→寺：01676_tera⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|ある}いて→歩く：00538_aruku⟧⟦{回|まわ}る→回る：01150_mawaru⟧⟦{巡礼|じゅんれい}→巡礼：10662_junrei⟧だ。
examples.english: The Shikoku pilgrimage is a walk around 88 temples associated with Kūkai.

notes:
In everyday speech he is usually called お{大師|だいし}さん or {弘法|こうぼう}さん.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦{弘法|こうぼう}も{筆|ふで}の{誤|あやま}り→弘法も筆の誤り：29266_kouboumofudenoayamari⟧: even Kōbō makes a slip of the brush (even experts make mistakes)
- {弘法|こうぼう}⟦{筆|ふで}→筆：03601_fude⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{選|えら}ば→選ぶ：00835_erabu⟧ず: Kōbō does not choose his brush (a master does not blame his tools)
- {弘法大師|こうぼうだいし}: his posthumous title
- ⟦{四国|しこく}→四国：21447_shikoku⟧{遍路|へんろ}: the pilgrimage to 88 temples in Shikoku linked with him
